title: Subrectangle Queries Manager
description:
Implement the class `SubrectangleQueries` which receives an `m x n` integer matrix `rectangle` and supports two operations:

- `SubrectangleQueries(int[][] rectangle)` initializes the object with the initial matrix.
- `void updateSubrectangle(int row1, int col1, int row2, int col2, int newValue)` overwrites every cell in the subrectangle with upper-left corner `(row1, col1)` and lower-right corner `(row2, col2)` inclusive with `newValue`.
- `int getValue(int row, int col)` returns the current value at coordinate `(row, col)`.
constraints: 0 <= row1 <= row2 < m, 0 <= col1 <= col2 < n
At most 500 operations will be called in total.
hints: Instead of rewriting up to m * n cells on every updateSubrectangle call, simply append the tuple (row1, col1, row2, col2, newValue) to an update history list in O(1).
To answer getValue(row, col), scan the history list from newest to oldest and return the first newValue whose bounding box covers (row, col), falling back to the original rectangle.

examples.explanation: Initially (0,2)=1; after overwriting [0..3, 0..2] with 5, both (0,2) and (3,1) return 5; then overwriting [3..3, 0..2] with 10 changes (3,1) to 10 while (0,2) remains 5.
Overlapping subrectangle updates resolve in reverse chronological order so the most recent write wins.
On a 1x1 rectangle, each update directly replaces the sole element.
